r1_risk_change: Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024; INE, Estadística Continua de Población (1 July); DGT, Censo de conductores 2014–2025; DGT registered vehicle fleet; CORES, consumo de productos petrolíferos. Period: 2019 and 2024, all roads. Definition: each outcome divided by each denominator in turn, as the ratio of the 2024 rate to the 2019 rate, with 95% log-normal intervals that treat both counts as Poisson and the denominators as known; count is the outcome with no denominator; road fuel is automotive petrol plus diesel in tonnes, a proxy for vehicle-kilometres; each panel has its own scale.
l2_observed_over_trend: Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024; DGT registered vehicle fleet; CORES, consumo de productos petrolíferos. Period: 2010–2024. Definition: 30-day deaths divided by the fitted (to 2019) or projected (from 2020) trend of each measure; 1 means on trend; shaded: the range of the ratio that the trend's 95% prediction interval allows, which is narrow where the trend was fitted and widens as the projection runs on.
l1_trend_projection: Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024; DGT registered vehicle fleet; CORES, consumo de productos petrolíferos. Period: 1993–2024 (road fuel from 1996). Definition: segmented log-linear (joinpoint) quasi-Poisson trends fitted to 30-day deaths up to 2019, turning points chosen by QBIC (deaths: 2003, 2013; deaths per registered vehicle: 2003, 2012; deaths per tonne of road fuel: 2002, 2011); the per-vehicle and per-fuel trends are multiplied back by each year's fleet or fuel so that all three panels are in deaths; shaded: 95% prediction interval of the projection.
m1_season_profile: Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024; CORES, consumo de productos petrolíferos; Ministerio de Transportes y Movilidad Sostenible, tráfico en autopistas estatales de peaje. Period: 2014–2019 and 2022–2024 (2020 and 2021 left out). Definition: each month's 30-day deaths, road fuel (petrol plus diesel), petrol alone and toll-motorway average daily traffic per kilometre, divided by the mean month of the same year and averaged across years.
m2_month_effects: Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024; CORES, consumo de productos petrolíferos; Ministerio de Transportes y Movilidad Sostenible, tráfico en autopistas estatales de peaje. Period: 2014–2019 and 2022–2024. Definition: month effects from quasi-Poisson models of monthly 30-day deaths with year effects; the first panel has no exposure, the others take the log of one traffic series as an offset, so their month effects are deaths per unit of that traffic against the average month; whiskers are 95% intervals on the overdispersed scale.
m3_lockdown: Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024; CORES, consumo de productos petrolíferos; Ministerio de Transportes y Movilidad Sostenible, tráfico en autopistas estatales de peaje. Period: 2020 against the 2017–2019 mean of each month. Definition: proportional change in 30-day deaths and in each traffic series; the state of alarm began on 14 March 2020 and the strictest restrictions ran to early May.
a3_sex_ratios: Source: DGT, Accidentes con víctimas, tablas estadísticas 2014–2024; DGT, Censo de conductores 2014–2025. Period: 2022–2024 pooled. Definition: car drivers involved in injury crashes and killed within 30 days (DGT tables 4.2 and 4.1.1, car rows), against licence-holder-years from the driver census and against the drivers involved; each row is the male rate divided by the female rate, with 95% log-normal intervals; drivers of unknown sex or age left out. n = 290,654 drivers involved.
f1_speed_severity: Source: DGT, Informe temático Factor Velocidad 2014–2023; DGT, Ficheros de microdatos de accidentes con víctimas 2016–2024. Period: 2016–2023 pooled, Spain without Cataluña and País Vasco. Definition: deaths within 30 days per 100 injury crashes in which the police recorded inappropriate speed as a concurrent factor, divided by the same ratio for the other injury crashes of the same road type and scope (totals from the microdata restricted to the report's provinces); 95% log-normal intervals; the adjusted row is a quasi-Poisson model with road type and year. n = 45,192 speed-related crashes.
f2_factor_shares: Source: DGT, Informe temático Factor Velocidad 2014–2023. Period: 2014–2023, Spain without Cataluña and País Vasco. Definition: injury crashes in which the police recorded each concurrent factor, as a share of all injury crashes in the zone; a line is broken wherever the share jumps or falls by more than 25% in one year (a recording break), so each unbroken run can be compared within itself; each panel has its own scale.
c3_speed_status: Source: DGT, Accidentes con víctimas, tablas estadísticas 2014–2024. Period: 2014–2024. Definition: drivers involved in injury crashes by the police's record of a speed infraction (yearbook tables 6.1); the top band is the share for which no judgement was recorded at all, which changes in 2016 and changes the meaning of every share below it. n = 1,794,406 drivers.
s1_forest_fatal: Source: DGT, Ficheros de microdatos de accidentes con víctimas 2016–2024. Period: 2016–2024. Definition: logistic regression of at least one death on the circumstances shown plus year; odds ratios against the reference level (hollow marker) with 95% intervals clustered by province; road surface 'not specified' (547 crashes) has no crash of this outcome, so it cannot be estimated and is left out of the plot. n = 875,013 crashes.
s2_adverse_conditions: Source: DGT, Ficheros de microdatos de accidentes con víctimas 2016–2024. Period: 2016–2024. Definition: odds of at least one death, given an injury crash, at each level against its reference; the first row is the full model and the others drop a correlated predictor or fit one kind of road on its own; a missing row is a level the variant does not contain; 95% intervals clustered by province; each panel has its own horizontal scale from zero. n = 875,013 crashes.
a1_km_risk_by_age: Source: DGT, Accidentes con víctimas, tablas estadísticas 2014–2024; DGT, Kilómetros anualizados recorridos por el parque móvil 2024. Period: 2024. Definition: car drivers involved in injury crashes and killed within 30 days (DGT tables 4.1.1 and 4.2, car rows only), against the kilometres driven in 2024 by cars whose registered owner is in the band; whiskers are exact 95% Poisson intervals on the counts, with the kilometres treated as known; each panel has its own horizontal scale from zero. n = 98,369 drivers involved.
a2_denominator_contrast: Source: DGT, Accidentes con víctimas, tablas estadísticas 2014–2024; DGT, Kilómetros anualizados recorridos por el parque móvil 2024; INE, Estadística Continua de Población; DGT, Censo de conductores. Period: 2024. Definition: car-driver deaths within 30 days divided by each denominator in turn and expressed as a ratio to the 35–54 band, with 95% log-normal intervals; the numerator is the same in every panel, so the movement between panels is the denominator and nothing else.
v1_per_vehicle_vs_per_km: Source: DGT, Accidentes con víctimas, tablas estadísticas 2014–2024; DGT, Kilómetros recorridos estimados a partir de la ITV 2022. Period: 2022. Definition: vehicles of each type involved in 30-day fatal crashes per 100,000 circulating vehicles (left) and per billion vehicle-km (right); the lines show how each type's rank moves when distance driven replaces fleet size as the denominator.
p1_points_series: Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024. Period: January 2000 to November 2007, all roads. Definition: deaths within 30 days of the crash; fitted = Poisson regression with month-of-year terms, a level and slope change at July 2006 and a pre-trend with a knot at Aug 2003 chosen by AIC on the months before the break; the dashed line is that model with the change set to zero and the dotted line the same counterfactual under one straight pre-trend, the specification that gives the larger drop. n = 38,852 deaths.
p2_july_placebos: Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024. Period: July of every year with a clean window, 1993–2024. Definition: the same segmented regression with the break placed at 1 July of each year, on a window of the same shape every time (60 months before, 17 after); the filled marker is July 2006 and the hollow ones are Julys the points licence cannot have affected; years whose window would contain July 2006 or the pandemic are left out. n = 15 fits.
d1_missingness: Source: DGT, Ficheros de microdatos de accidentes con víctimas 2016–2024. Period: 2016–2024. Definition: observed = not empty, not 999 (not specified), not 998 (not applicable) and not an explicit unknown code. The fields that carry no code list count their placeholder values as not observed too: KM 9999 (and 1000 in 2019, the year DGT used it), CARRETERA 'No inventariada' and COD_MUNICIPIO 00000. n = 875,013 crashes.
